summary: The tests are syntactically correct and use Playwright APIs properly, ensuring compilation and runtime correctness. Await is used correctly with assertions, and Locators are handled appropriately. However, selectors rely on data-test attributes without clarity about their stability, and navigation validation only checks a partial URL match, which is weak against false positives. Additionally, test titles do not include testCaseId references, which reduces traceability. No hard-coded waits or placeholder URLs were used.

issues.description: Selectors are based only on data-test attributes like [data-test="product-1"]. While better than generic selectors, these could be weak if such attributes are not stable or consistently applied.
issues.recommendation: Verify that data-test attributes are stable and consistently applied; consider stronger selectors or role-based selectors if suitable.

issues.description: The navigation assertion checks only url matching /product/, which is a weak validation and can produce false positives if the url contains 'product' but is not the intended product detail page.
issues.recommendation: Enhance URL assertion to check full expected product detail page URL or validate presence of unique page elements on the product detail page.

issues.description: Test titles do not include testCaseId values (TC-001, TC-003), reducing traceability between manual and automated tests.
issues.recommendation: Include testCaseId identifiers in test titles to improve traceability and reporting.

recommendations: Improve URL validation to assert full expected URLs or page-specific unique elements after navigation.
Ensure data-test attributes used in selectors are stable and well maintained.
Include testCaseId values in test titles for better traceability.
